name: Online booking widget for local trades
one_liner: An embeddable website and Google Business booking widget that lets customers see and book trade services (electricians, mechanics) without emailing back and forth.
customer: Small trade businesses: electricians, mechanics, plumbers and other service trades
offer: A SaaS widget that lists services visually, takes bookings and links to Google reservations, with backend automations
how_it_makes_money: Monthly SaaS subscription. Per-customer pricing not stated.
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; about $40K/month within roughly 1 year of launch
evidence: 'We do 85,000 a month in revenue now, in Australian dollars' (mr4YV-9MY0Q)
'an anonymous startup making over $40,000 a month launched just about a year ago' (mr4YV-9MY0Q)
Solves 'I have money, I want to buy from a service business. Why do I have to send them an email?' (mr4YV-9MY0Q)
risks: Trades are slow to adopt software and may need hands-on onboarding
Competition from Calendly-style tools and booking features built into existing platforms
The growth tactic for the first 10 customers isn't detailed in the digest

name: Niche daily web game network
one_liner: A simple daily browser game cloned across many niches (e.g. sports geography: 'tap where it happened'), earning from a large user base.
customer: Fans of specific niches (NFL and other sports fans). Revenue likely comes from advertisers, but this isn't stated.
offer: Free daily web games, one per niche, all built on the same engine
how_it_makes_money: About $40K/month from about 700K monthly active users. The exact model isn't stated; likely ads.
startup_cost: low (built in a weekend with Claude)
time_to_first_revenue: Weeks: a couple of thousand dollars a month early on, $40K/month within about 3 months
evidence: 'I built this game in just a weekend, and we make about $40,000 monthly' (s9aLA4IOSZE)
'They're all the same game just for different niches' (s9aLA4IOSZE)
risks: Results are hit-driven and depend on going viral
Ad revenue is volatile
Easy for others to copy

name: Amazon Influencer video reviews
one_liner: Record short product review videos for Amazon listings and earn commission on sales they drive.
customer: Amazon pays the commission; the buyers are Amazon shoppers
offer: Product review videos (face optional) uploaded through the Amazon Influencer program
how_it_makes_money: Affiliate commission on sales. Cases cited: $10K/month working 4–5 hrs/week, $12K/month part-time, $40K in one month with about 1,100 videos.
time_to_first_revenue: Weeks; one beginner made $700 in their first week
evidence: 'I'm making over $10,000 per month, but I work no more than four to five hours per week' (nVgFbclwmSA)
'he has about 1,100 and just last month, he did $40,000' (nVgFbclwmSA)
risks: Depends entirely on Amazon's commission rates and policies
Income figures come from a promoter of a related tool, so they may be biased
Availability and earnings in the UK programme are unverified

name: Airbnb co-hosting for property owners
one_liner: Manage other people's short-term rentals for a cut of revenue, with no property purchase needed.
offer: Listing management, guest messaging, pricing and coordinating cleaners
how_it_makes_money: Percentage of booking revenue (rate not stated). Example: 10–20 co-host clients within about 6 months.
evidence: 'better option for no money down… would be through co-hosting' (pKja9oxDAaQ)
'some people that have gotten 10-20 co-host clients in a short six months' (pKja9oxDAaQ)
risks: Needs local cleaners and maintenance on the ground
Short-let regulations in the UK and Portugal (e.g. AL licensing)
Revenue is seasonal

name: Unique-themed short-term rental
one_liner: A differentiated experience rental (e.g. a converted barn for family groups) that books at high prices and builds a waitlist.
customer: Families and groups looking for experience stays
offer: An experience-led rental with large group capacity
how_it_makes_money: Nightly bookings averaging $4–5K per booking. $200K booked within 45 days of launch, $300K within 3 months.
startup_cost: high (property purchase and renovation, funded from savings and lines of credit)
evidence: '$500 into one Instagram ad… some days five to six bookings a day' (pKja9oxDAaQ)
'average booking size is somewhere between $4 to $5,000' (pKja9oxDAaQ)
risks: Needs heavy capital
Requires physical operations
Doesn't fit the low-cost, async goal

name: Replenishable consumable subscription brand
one_liner: A subscription brand for a consumable product (e.g. functional coffee), made by a contract manufacturer.
offer: Monthly subscription deliveries, with retail and Amazon as extra channels
how_it_makes_money: Recurring subscription revenue: $11K MRR, with subscribers staying 7–8 months on average
evidence: 'on average over seven or eight months' retention (oSk1xDrgqBY)
Founders admit they were 'just breaking even' (oSk1xDrgqBY)
risks: Customer acquisition costs and shipping eat into margins
Requires inventory
Organic certification costs time and money

name: Liquidation pallet reselling
one_liner: Buy Amazon and other retail return pallets and resell the items individually on eBay.
how_it_makes_money: Selling price minus pallet cost: 3 pallets for $1,500, with some items selling for $40–80 each. Profit isn't proven.
startup_cost: low-medium (about $1,500 for 3 pallets, plus storage space)
evidence: Weak evidence: 'bought 3 Amazon return pallets for $1,500'; the creator says 'it's not really about making money' (orDRxYfVypw)
risks: Labour-heavy
Pallet contents are unpredictable
Margins are thin
